title: Stream watermarking: eliminate duplicate tokens & truncated JSON on reconnects
creator: Marta Lopez
description:
Summary:
A set of Hosted API customers reported two correlated issues during intermittent network flaps: (1) duplicate tokens emitted after reconnecting to a stream and (2) truncated JSON objects as the final chunk, causing downstream parsers to error. These manifested primarily on HTTP/2 connection reuse scenarios and when the request routed to a different replica during a fallback.

Root cause hypothesis and findings:
- The current resume protocol relies on an opaque byte-offset + KV-cache expectations. When a request is rerouted to another replica that had a KV cache eviction (or different prefix compacting), the resumed output diverged.
- The proxy-layer attempted optimistic local replay of the last N bytes, resulting in overlapping tokens when the server also replayed content.
- Finalization (closing bracket/token) was sometimes emitted by the original server but lost in the handoff path, leaving clients with truncated JSON.
- Observability gaps: no monotonic stream sequence id was recorded at the proxy edge, making postmortem of which side sent what difficult.

Proposed fix (high level):
1) Introduce a per-stream monotonic watermark (stream_seq_id) assigned at proxy ingress and included in every SSE event/frame metadata.
2) Extend the resume handshake to include the last-acked stream_seq_id from the client. The server will only replay tokens with seq_id > last_acked. This prevents double-replay races.
3) Add a definitive "finalization marker" event (event: stream.done, seq_id: X, signature) that is idempotent and verified by the client; proxies will persist the finalization marker for a short TTL to ensure replay safety during immediate reconnects.
4) Instrument KV cache eviction telemetry and route-fallback events to correlated traces so we can observe mismatches.

Planned changes and scope:
- Runtime change: include stream_seq_id in the runtime transport layer and wire into SSE encoder. (ENG + runtime infra)
- Proxy change: assign watermark and persist last-finalization markers for active stream sessions. (edge team)
- Client SDK guidance: update SDK to include seq ack in reconnect handshake and tolerate the stream.done marker. (DX)
- Backfill: add integration tests that fuzz network flaps, replica switchovers, and cache eviction to validate no duplicates and valid JSON closure.

Risks and mitigations:
- Backward compatibility: older SDKs won't understand stream_seq_id. Mitigate by keeping existing resume semantics if no seq_id present and adding conservative safety windows (e.g., server will detect potential overlap and only allow replay up to N tokens).
- Performance: adding metadata increases per-event bytes; we'll encode compactly and evaluate CPU impact in staging.
- Complexity across Dedicated/Private: Private customers may have different proxy topology; the protocol is opt-in via a runtime flag and will be rolled to Dedicated/Private after hosted validation.
acceptance_criteria: No duplicate tokens observed in 99.99th percentile under simulated 1s-10s network flaps in integration tests
Clients reconnecting mid-stream must receive a complete, parseable JSON payload ending with stream.done when generation completes
No increase >5% in median per-token latency in staging with stream_seq_id enabled
Observability dashboards show stream_seq_id and finalization marker events correlated with route-fallback traces
implementation_plan: Design proto: add stream_seq_id (u64) and finalization marker to SSE event schema - RFC by 2026-03-12
Runtime patch: encode stream_seq_id on token frames and honor resume seq in server replay logic - branch: feat/stream-watermark
Proxy patch: assign watermark at ingress, persist finalization markers in memstore (TTL 60s), and include seq_id in reconnect handshake
SDK updates: JS/Go SDKs accept and send last_acked_seq on reconnect; expose stream.done semantics
Integration tests: add flaky-network harness and run 10k randomized reconnects
Canary rollout: enable on 10% of hosted edge, monitor errors and dup-token metric for 72h
Full rollout if canary meets acceptance criteria
qa_checks: Unit tests for seq monotonicity and gap detection
End-to-end test with simulated replica switch and KV eviction scenario
Fuzz harness ensuring JSON closure even when reconnect occurs during last token emission
Performance benchmark comparing before/after per-token latency and CPU
